// THE BLOCK-SCOPE DEFEAT, found by a review that wrote it into PRODUCTION code and
// watched this gate stay green.
//
// wireEnv opens a lexical scope for a *ast.FuncLit and for nothing else, so two
// blocks of one function body — an if/else, two switch cases, two select comm
// clauses, a workflow.GetVersion's two arms — shared one scope key, and e.decls was
// last-write-wins. okReceiveTarget reads that map AFTER index() has finished, so the
// declared type it judged a receive by was the LAST `var <name>` in the body, not the
// one in scope at the receive.
//
// ShadowedSilencer is the reviewer's shape, transcribed from the production file it
// was written into (manager/delivery/projectsupervision.go:55, this gate's own
// mutation-1 site): a struct receive target, and four lines later, inside an `if`, a
// `var raw any` that names the same local and is used for nothing. It compiled, it
// vetted, it linted, and the gate reported "12 channels (6 bus), 5 producers, 9
// receive targets" — the vacuity log unchanged — while the operator-pause receive it
// exists to guard dropped every relayed message.
//
// TwoArmedFence is the same hole written by ACCIDENT rather than on purpose, and it
// is why this fixture is not a curiosity: it is the natural two-arm GetVersion shape,
// a pre-change arm holding a struct and a new arm normalising into `var raw any` of
// the same name. Stage 4b3 Task 3 discharged the last of those fences; a future wave
// will add one back, and under the old map the NEW arm would have silenced the OLD
// one — the exact instance bad_fenced.go.txt exists to keep red.
//
// THREE findings, and the third is the FIX'S OWN COST, pinned here rather than left
// to be discovered. declare() now resolves a same-name conflict toward NOT-`any`, so
// TwoArmedFence's two receives are BOTH judged against operatorPauseSignal: the
// pre-change arm truly (it is a struct target), and the new arm SPURIOUSLY, because
// the gate cannot tell the two locals apart. That false positive is the price of
// being construct-blind instead of enumerating block kinds, it is remedied by
// renaming one local, and it is the direction this file resolves every uncertainty
// in — see blind spot 4 in signalwire_arch_test.go's header.
package badshadowed

const signalOperatorPauseRequested = "operatorPauseRequested"

type operatorPauseSignal struct {
	ProjectID string
	Reason    string
}

func ShadowedSilencer(ctx workflow.Context) (string, bool) {
	pauseCh := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	var raw operatorPauseSignal
	pauseCh.Receive(ctx, &raw) // WANT: flagged — a struct target, silenced by the block below
	reason, decoded := raw.Reason, raw.Reason != ""
	if !decoded {
		var raw any
		_ = raw
	}
	return reason, decoded
}

func TwoArmedFence(ctx workflow.Context) (string, bool) {
	ch := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	if workflow.GetVersion(ctx, "a-future-fence", workflow.DefaultVersion, 1) < 1 {
		// The PRE-CHANGE arm, written first, as a real fence is.
		var raw operatorPauseSignal
		ch.Receive(ctx, &raw) // WANT: flagged — a struct target the new arm used to silence
		return raw.Reason, raw.Reason != ""
	}
	// The NEW arm, correct on its own terms.
	var raw any
	ch.Receive(ctx, &raw) // WANT: flagged SPURIOUSLY — the documented cost, see the header
	return normaliseShadowed(raw)
}

// ClosureSilencer is THE SAME DEFEAT ONE CONSTRUCT FURTHER OUT, and it survived the first
// fix. declare's conflict rule holds within one scope KEY, and index() opens a scope per
// *ast.FuncLit — so the outer struct and the inner `any` are two keys, never a collision,
// and lookupDecl's innermost-first walk let the inner one answer. It built, vetted, linted
// clean and left the gate PASS with its vacuity log unchanged at 12/6/5/9 when written into
// projectsupervision.go. The `workflow.Go(ctx, func(gctx workflow.Context) {…})` spelling
// silences it identically, and was measured to.
//
// Go's own scoping is what makes this a true defeat and not a curiosity: the inner `raw`
// comes into force only AFTER its ValueSpec, so `&raw` at the Receive genuinely is the outer
// struct, and the message is genuinely dropped in production.
//
// lookupDecl now returns the STRICTEST declaration on the chain rather than the innermost,
// which is declare's rule stated ALONG the chain instead of across one scope. Revert either
// half and this fixture goes quiet.
func ClosureSilencer(ctx workflow.Context) (string, bool) {
	ch := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, signalOperatorPauseRequested)
	var raw operatorPauseSignal
	func() {
		ch.Receive(ctx, &raw) // WANT: flagged — &raw is the OUTER struct, whatever the line below says
		var raw any
		_ = raw
	}()
	return raw.Reason, raw.Reason != ""
}

func normaliseShadowed(raw any) (string, bool) {
	s, ok := raw.(string)
	return s, ok
}
